reason: Code written to follow the layering and dependency-direction rules.
A domain policy touching infrastructure only through a Protocol given to its constructor is not reaching for infrastructure itself.
A repository whose declared job is talking to a database is the correct home for SQL.
A base class calling its own abstract method, overridden by a subclass, points the dependency the right way.
A function whose sole purpose is assembling an object graph is where construction belongs.
Building a small immutable value object inline is not assembling an infrastructure collaborator.
Methods returning different shapes because the operations differ (lookup, bulk query, count) are not a missing convention.
A layer reaching into one it must not; the fixture was written to violate that.
The general depending on the specific; the fixture was written to violate that.
Building collaborators and using them in the same place; the fixture was written to violate that.
The same kind of operation done in different ways; the fixture was written to violate that.
Priority-tier fixture built as a clear high.
Priority-tier fixture built as a clear medium.
Priority-tier fixture built as a clear low.
A business rule duplicated across two layers is architecture-adjacent but outside ARCH's four categories, so it is reported only at low.
